session1: Some background before we start. Our app runs on this fork with the Prisma adapter, but only so users can link several OAuth accounts to one user. Sessions stay JWT. We ran database sessions for a month last quarter and rejected them: every middleware check went to Postgres from the Edge runtime, which can't hold a connection pool, and p95 latency hit 900 ms. Can you find where the session strategy gets its default?
OK, that's the line I was thinking of. Keep the decision in mind; it matters when we wire the adapter in.
tasks.session2: I'm adding `adapter: PrismaAdapter(prisma)` to our Auth.js config today. Which session strategy should we end up on, and what, if anything, do I need to add to the config for it? Finish with one line in exactly this form: ANSWER: strategy=<jwt or database>; config=<what to add, or none>
tasks.oracle: Decision: sessions stay JWT even though the Prisma adapter is configured; the adapter is there only for account linking. Database sessions were tried for a month and rejected: middleware hit Postgres from the Edge runtime, which cannot pool connections, and p95 latency reached 900 ms. packages/core/src/lib/init.ts defaults the strategy to "database" whenever an adapter is set, so the config must say session: { strategy: "jwt" } explicitly.
tasks.reference:
With an adapter, init.ts defaults the strategy to database, but we decided to stay on JWT, so it has to be set explicitly.
ANSWER: strategy=jwt; config=session: { strategy: "jwt" }

Which of our files import the vendored cookie module?

session1: Background on cookie size. Users who belong to many groups were hitting our ingress's 8 KB request-header limit. We tried lowering CHUNK_SIZE in packages/core/src/lib/utils/cookie.ts so each session-cookie chunk is smaller. Dead end: smaller chunks only meant more chunks, the total Cookie header grew because each chunk repeats its name and attributes, and Safari began dropping the last chunks. We reverted it. What worked was trimming the token in our `jwt` callback: keep only the user id and role, and load groups on the server. Can you show me how the chunking works?
Right. So the chunk size stays as it is; trimming the token is the approach.
tasks.session2: A new enterprise customer's users get `431 Request Header Fields Too Large` right after sign-in; their tokens carry hundreds of group claims. What change do you propose? Finish with one line in exactly this form: ANSWER: change=<the one change you propose, and where>
tasks.oracle: Dead end: lowering CHUNK_SIZE in packages/core/src/lib/utils/cookie.ts to make session-cookie chunks smaller was tried and reverted. It produced more chunks and a larger total Cookie header (each chunk repeats its name and attributes), and Safari dropped the last chunks. What worked: trim the token in the jwt callback to the user id and role, and load groups on the server.
tasks.reference:
Smaller chunks were tried and made the header bigger.
ANSWER: change=trim the token in the jwt callback to user id and role, and load groups on the server

session1: Ops wants to cut how often we rewrite the session cookie. Before they change anything: for JWT sessions, how and where does the expiry get pushed back when a session is used, and does session.updateAge throttle it? Please trace it in the code rather than going by the docs.
Interesting. Keep that finding; ops will come back to it.
tasks.session2: Ops plans to set `session.updateAge` to 3600 so the JWT session cookie is rewritten at most once an hour. Will that work? Finish with one line in exactly this form: ANSWER: throttles_jwt=<yes or no>; file=<the file that refreshes the JWT session>
tasks.oracle: Finding from tracing the code: in packages/core/src/lib/actions/session.ts a JWT session is re-encoded (jwt.encode) with a new expiry from fromDate(sessionMaxAge), and its cookie is set again, on every session request. session.updateAge is read only in the database-strategy branch, where it throttles database writes; it does not throttle JWT sessions, whatever its doc comment suggests.
tasks.reference:
updateAge is read only in the database branch of session.ts; the JWT branch re-encodes on every request.
ANSWER: throttles_jwt=no; file=packages/core/src/lib/actions/session.ts
